Next: the web app — the demo judges will open. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 3–8, 11 and the demo plan below are the spec; the backend from the previous task (sweep, store, trace, repair pipeline, verdict rules, i18n) already works — build the UI and a small HTTP server on top of it, do not rewrite it. Follow AGENTS.md. Live Spark/SAM calls allowed (a few cents); never call the Graph API with --execute and never import any Graph write function into the web server. Do not commit or push. Everything bilingual (English default, Hebrew toggle, RTL when Hebrew).

## Demo plan this serves (decided)
Judging: Impact 30%, use of Meta tooling 25%, technical 20%, demo 25%. A judge opens the live site and within 20 seconds must understand: the approved offer changed, some ads still promise the old deal, Offer Guard found them with evidence, fixed only the offer panel with pixel proof (product and logo did not move a single pixel), refused when unsafe, flagged the landing page instead of "fixing" a correct ad, and asked one question when unclear. Our synthetic GALI campaign is already swept (saved results, labeled with capture time) with one "Run fresh analysis" button. A bounded "Check your own ad" lets judges try it. Publishing a PAUSED ad is owner-only and comes in the next task — not here.

Design direction: clean, calm, few words, big numbers, tooltips instead of paragraphs. It must look like a real product, not a debug page. Works on a phone (390 px) and a laptop (1440 px). Every label honest: "fresh" / "saved · captured <time>" / "synthetic fictional brand".

## 1. Stack (keep it small — it runs on a shared 8 GB server)
- Server: Hono + `@hono/node-server` in `src/server/http/` (app factory `createApp(deps)` so tests can run it in-process). Binds `127.0.0.1`, port `OFFER_GUARD_PORT` (default 3023). All routes work under a base path `OFFER_GUARD_BASE_PATH` (default `/`; production will be `/offer-guard/` behind nginx) — the frontend uses relative URLs only.
- Frontend: no framework. TypeScript in `src/web/`, bundled with esbuild to `dist/web/` (`npm run build:web`), plus one CSS file. A tiny `h()` DOM helper is fine. Model/page/ad text is always set with `textContent` — never `innerHTML` with data.
- Fonts: the bundled Noto Sans + Noto Sans Hebrew from `@fontsource` (already installed), served from our server. No CDN, no external request of any kind (CSP `default-src 'self'`, no inline scripts, `img-src 'self' data: blob:`).
- `npm run web` (build + start), `npm run web:dev` (rebuild on change). Update `.env.example` with the new vars (no secrets there).

## 2. Read API (public, read-only)
- `GET /api/campaign` → approved offer spec (current version), latest run: id, mode (fresh/cached), started/finished time, counts per verdict and per language, and one row per ad: id, lang, thumbnail URL, verdict, one-line reason (i18n key + vars, not English text), cache state, capture time.
- `GET /api/ads/:id` → everything for the detail view: spec; ad claims with verbatim quotes and source bbox; page claims with verified quotes, bboxes and capture screenshot refs; field-by-field comparison (spec · ad · page, status per field); findings; verdict + explanation key; the AMBIGUOUS question; repair artifact (before/after/panel/masks/diff refs, proof numbers, digest, spec version, revalidation result with the fresh Spark claims) or refusal blockers; trace events.
- `GET /api/runs/:id/trace` → the run's trace.
- Images/artifacts are served **by record id** (`/media/:kind/:id`), resolved through the DB to a path that must stay inside the artifacts/data dirs (realpath check). The client never sends a file path. `fixtures/pages/` is served read-only at `/pages/` (these are the GALI landing pages; later the seeded ads will link to them).
- Errors return JSON `{error: <i18n key>}`; never stack traces.

## 3. Screens
**a. Campaign (home).** Header: Offer Guard + one-line tagline + EN/עב toggle (remember choice in localStorage, `?lang=` wins). Approved-offer card (20% off selected models · until 10.11.2026 · paid shipping) with spec version. Five big verdict counters (CLEAN, AD WRONG · FIXED, AD WRONG · REFUSED, PAGE WRONG, NEEDS ANSWER) that also filter the grid. Language filter (All / English / Hebrew). Grid of ad cards: image, verdict badge (color + icon + word — never color alone), one-line reason, small "saved · captured …" / "fresh". "Run fresh analysis" button → live progress per ad (SSE `GET /api/jobs/:id/events`, fall back to polling) and the grid updates as ads finish. A short 3-step strip "Read the ad → Check the page → Fix only the offer panel" with tooltips.
**b. Ad detail.** Verdict banner with plain explanation. Three-column evidence (stacks on mobile): Approved offer · What the ad says (quote + zoomed crop of the source bbox) · What the landing page says (quote + crop of the capture with the quote's bbox highlighted, link to the live page). Comparison table per field (discount, scope, shipping, valid until) with ✓ / ✗ / ? per source. Then, by verdict:
  - AD_WRONG_REPAIRABLE → repair view: before/after slider (and a toggle for keyboard users), overlay toggle for SAM masks (product + logo, labeled), changed-pixel heatmap (magenta = changed, green = protected), three big proof numbers: "0 px changed in protected areas", "0 px changed outside the offer panel", "re-check by a fresh Spark call: PASS" with its extracted fields; digest + spec version; download after.png. A note: "Pixel identity is for our exported PNG; Meta may recompress after upload." A disabled "Create PAUSED replacement ad" button with tooltip "owner only — signed-in view".
  - AD_WRONG_UNSAFE → refusal: the blockers in plain words, the SAM overlay showing where the panel overlaps the product (or why the panel is not opaque).
  - PAGE_WRONG → "The ad is right; the landing page is not. We flag it and do not change the ad." with the page evidence highlighted. Also show that the injected line on the page was treated as data (it is visible on the page capture).
  - AMBIGUOUS → the one focused question, prominent.
  - CLEAN → "No contradiction found in this ad and its page" (not "approved").
**c. Trace drawer** (on detail, collapsible, closed by default): the real recorded tool-call timeline — step, model or tool (show the model id: `muse-spark-1.3`, `sam-3.1`, Playwright, Sharp, code), concise input → output, duration, link to the evidence, next state, cached/fresh. No invented "reasoning" text. A header line counts calls per Meta model.
**d. Check your own ad.** Upload one JPEG/PNG (+ optional ad copy), edit the offer spec fields (prefilled with GALI's spec), pick a landing page **only from our GALI pages** (dropdown; say plainly "arbitrary URLs are disabled in this demo"). Runs the same pipeline (verdict + repair + proof when allowed) and shows the same detail view. Never publishes. Uploads: decode with sharp, JPEG/PNG only by content (not extension), ≤5 MB, ≤12 MP, re-encode to strip metadata, stored under `data/uploads/` and deleted after 24 h (cleanup on start + hourly), never under the repo's tracked dirs.
**e. About** (short): how it works in 5 steps with the Meta model used at each step, honest limits (synthetic fixtures, our own test account, single-image ads, one panel family), link to the GitHub repo and docs/build/BUILD_LOG.md.

## 4. Spend and abuse limits (anything that calls a model)
- Kill switch `OFFER_GUARD_LIVE=off` → fresh runs and own-ad checks return a friendly "live analysis paused; showing saved results" (saved results keep working).
- One heavy job at a time (fresh sweep or own-ad check), queue ≤3, else "busy, try in a minute". Hard timeout per job.
- Per IP: 3 live jobs per hour (trust `X-Forwarded-For` only when `OFFER_GUARD_TRUST_PROXY=1`). Global daily cap on model calls `OFFER_GUARD_DAILY_MODEL_CALLS` (default 300), counted in SQLite; over the cap → kill-switch message.
- Cache: the existing cache key (image + copy + URL + spec + models + prompt versions) — a fresh sweep re-runs models, an own-ad check of an identical input returns the cached result labeled as such.
- Body limits on every POST; reject unknown fields (zod).

## 5. Tests (no network)
API tests in-process with a temp DB seeded from fixtures (no model calls): campaign/detail shapes, base-path routing, media path traversal (`../`, encoded, symlink) → 404, upload validation (wrong type by content, too big, too many pixels, polyglot), rate limit + queue + kill switch + daily cap, CSP and security headers present, every UI string exists in both languages (key parity test), the web server module graph does not import `src/server/meta/graph` write functions or `scripts/seed-campaign`.

## 6. Run and look at it yourself
- Build, start against the real `data/offer-guard.db`, and drive it with Playwright: screenshots of home, a repaired ad, the refused ad, the PAGE_WRONG ad, the AMBIGUOUS ad, the trace drawer open, and Check your own ad — each in English and Hebrew, at 1440×900 and 390×844 → `artifacts/ui/` (gitignored). Fail on any console error or failed request. Look at the screenshots and fix what looks broken (overflow, mixed-direction text, cut-off Hebrew, unreadable contrast).
- One live "Run fresh analysis" through the UI and one live "Check your own ad" with `fixtures/ads/ad-02-wrong-en.png` (a few cents). Batch live commands so you need as few approvals as possible.
- Then `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`. Update README (how to run the web app, env vars, what is public vs owner-only) and keep docs/ARCHITECTURE.md in sync if anything changed. Report: what was built, screenshots list, the live results, and anything you could not finish.
